The Major Culprit Right Now?
"Brent Crude"!

Brent crude is around $113 a barrel today & we all know that we imports nearly 90% of its oil. At these levels the obvious happens : import bill rises, the rupee comes under pressure, and company costs go up.
India brings in roughly 4.9 million barrels a day. A $10 rise that stays can add about $18 billion to the annual import bill. More dollars go out & a weaker rupee makes the next barrel costlier.

On 22 October, when Brent crossed $112, Nifty fell 0.54% and Sensex dropped 0.62%. Oil was not the only reason, but it added to the selling.
Higher diesel and petrol raise costs across transport, raw materials and manufacturing. Companies with stronger pricing power and reasonable valuations are better placed. Expensive mid and small caps with thin margins could face a double hit from lower earnings and falling valuations. Logistics, auto parts, building materials and a lot of mid and small manufacturers fall in the group that absorbs more of the cost. Revenues can still grow while margins get squeezed.

Yes Upstream oil & gas producers gain from higher prices, but they are a small part of the index and of most portfolios. The net effect for the broader market stays negative when oil stays high.
The market is already cutting stock prices before the weaker margins even show up in quarterly results. That is why the reaction looks broader than just the obvious oil-sensitive names.
If Brent stays above $110 for weeks, the chance of earnings downgrades in H2 FY27 rises and foreign flows stay cautious. A move back towards $100 would ease some of the pressure on earnings expectations and market sentiment. A few days of expensive oil is manageable,but several months is a totally different story !

✔️ The earlier rise and the current fall!

These stocks went up a lot in parts of 2024 and 2025-26. People put more money there because they were the ones still rising. Now a good part of that rise is coming back in a short time. The index being 12-13% down does not show the full picture. Many stocks that hit 52-week highs earlier this year are already 20-40% lower from those levels. In the Smallcap 250 many stocks have fallen more than the index itself.

✔️What it means for investors portfolios ! 

Most people do not own all 250 stocks. They own a few. When most of those few fall together, the portfolio falls more than the index number. During the correction from late 2024 to February 2025, the Midcap 150 fell around 20% and the Smallcap 250 about 25% before recovering. This time it is not that deep yet, but it has come fast and it has hit a lot of stocks at the same time. That is why the pain in many accounts feels larger than the index numbers suggest.

On 17 September, NTPC invoked ₹41.34 crore of Insurance Surety Bonds on a power contract. The full amount was paid the same day, according to Crisil's rating rationale on the contractor.

The contract was a ₹413 crore engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) package for 400 MWh of battery storage at NTPC's Mouda Super Thermal Power Station. NTPC awarded it to G R Infraprojects (GRIL) in March 2026. Six months in, GRIL issued a termination notice, citing force majeure and war risk linked to the West Asia conflict. NTPC says critical activities were delayed and treats the termination as a default by the contractor. GRIL has disputed the invocation, and the matter has gone to dispute resolution.

NTPC invoked ₹90.86 crore of security on 17 September, two days after GRIL's termination notice. This was a ₹49.53 crore mobilisation advance bank guarantee and ₹41.34 crore in Insurance Surety Bonds for performance security. Both were paid on the same day.

For insurers that issue Insurance Surety Bonds in India, three points stand out.

The insurer paid on the same day as the bank. A Maharatna company invoked an Insurance Surety Bond alongside a bank guarantee, and NTPC received both amounts on 17 September. Procurement teams now have a recorded case of an Insurance Surety Bond paying out on invocation alongside a bank guarantee.

The contractor was financially strong. GRIL is rated Crisil AA. Crisil reports that GRIL sought contractual relief because of market conditions after the West Asia conflict, and NTPC did not grant it. Insurers who price mainly on a contractor's financials would have seen a comfortable risk here. Force majeure clauses, price variation terms and tenor need the same scrutiny as the contractor's books.

The contractor repaid both issuers. Crisil reports that GRIL had kept funds with the bank and the insurer and honoured the full ₹90.86 crore on the same day. CARE Ratings reports that GRIL funded the amounts payable to both. Under a bank guarantee and an Insurance Surety Bond alike, the issuer pays the beneficiary and the contractor repays the issuer. Neither report says what margin, if any, the insurer held when it issued the bonds. 
That margin decides how much working capital a contractor frees by choosing an Insurance Surety Bond.

More storage contracts are coming. NTPC Green Energy (NGEL) invited bids in September for a 3.3 GWh storage project at Khavda, due on 27 October. NTPC told analysts after its Q4 FY26 results that about 5 GWh of storage is being built at its thermal stations, and Mouda was one of those projects. Insurers will be asked to issue Insurance Surety Bonds for performance security on these contracts.
